data.title: J.P. Morgan Assigns Hims & Hers Stock a 'Hold' Rating. What's Behind the Cautious Stance?
data.description:
J.P. Morgan analyst Bryan Smilek initiated coverage of telehealth platform Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) with a Hold rating and a price target of $32. The analyst is positive about the company's vertical integration, brand scale, and expansion across specialties and geographies. However, Smilek currently prefers to be on the sidelines as he looks for "execution across the strategic transition toward branded GLP-1s, durability of growth across newer specialties, deeper int'l penetration, & durable margin expansion."

J.P. Morgan Is Cautious on HIMS Stock

Smilek noted that Hims & Hers Health's five specialties (such as the GLP-1/weight loss business) generate more than $100 million in annual U.S. revenue, while three international markets (UK, Australia, and Germany) also generate over $100 million in annualized revenue. He highlighted that HIMS continues to rapidly expand its hormonal offerings for both men and women, as well as its Labs offerings.

Furthermore, the analyst noted that while most of the GLP-1 business was historically based on compounding treatments, HIMS announced a strategic shift in March under which the U.S. weight loss business will focus more on branded, FDA-approved treatments. While HIMS will no longer advertise compounded GLP-1 offerings, it will still offer them where clinically required.

Smilek expects the Novo partnership to more than offset compounded GLP-1 headwinds. He projects GLP-1 revenue to grow 46% to $1.1 billion in FY26 and constitute about 35% of HIMS' overall revenue. Smilek also noted the company's expansion into other specialties, such as peptides.

While Smilek discussed several positives, he is cautious on Hims & Hers Health as he awaits further evidence that the company can successfully transition to branded GLP-1s, sustain growth in newer specialties, and deliver continued margin improvement.

data.title: Tesla (TSLA) to Bring Its Semi Electric Truck to Europe in 2027
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) has confirmed that its Semi electric truck is coming to Europe, with customer deliveries set to begin in 2027. The EV giant introduced the adapted European model at the IAA Transportation show in Hannover. It also launched new regional web pages with the truck's specs, design updates, and key features.

The move marks Tesla's first big push for the Semi outside North America. The truck was first shown in 2017, but production faced long delays as Tesla focused battery supplies on its passenger cars. Limited U.S. deliveries began in late 2022, and Tesla said earlier this year that the first Semi had rolled off a high‑volume line in Nevada. Full production is now planned for 2026.

Tesla's European site lists a version with up to 550 km of range at a 40‑tonne weight, using about 1 kWh per kilometer. The truck weighs around 9,100 kg without cargo and offers 25 kW of electric power take‑off. Using Tesla's Megacharger network, the Semi can recover about 60% of its range in 30 minutes, with charging speeds up to 800 kW.

Promotion

TSLQ: built for a short position on TSLA

Tesla said the European Semi will come with route‑based charging plans and its own service centers to reduce downtime for fleet operators. The launch puts Tesla into a fast-growing European truck market where several truck makers already sell battery-powered heavy-duty models.

Key Details About Tesla Semi

The Tesla Semi is built as a Class 8 electric truck that beats standard diesel trucks in efficiency, running costs, and hill‑climbing power. The Semi uses a multi‑motor setup where one "torque axle" gives strong low‑speed power for pulling heavy loads uphill, and a second "efficiency axle" helps the truck cruise smoothly on highways.

The truck replaced old hydraulic assist with a fully electric power steering system. It maintains a physical link to the wheels. However, the setup gives a smoother steering feel and makes it easier to tie in Autopilot features.

Data from hundreds of pilot trucks that have logged over 13.5 million miles reflect the vehicle's advantages. During commercial freight testing, the Semi averaged an energy consumption of 1.55 to 1.7 kWh per mile at steady highway speeds. Thanks to its strong efficiency and low drag (about 0.4), the Semi is roughly 50% cheaper to run per mile than diesel trucks in high fuel-cost states like California, and about 20% cheaper nationwide.

Is Tesla Stock Good to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, TSLA stock has a Hold consensus rating based on 11 Buys, 12 Holds, and three Sells assigned in the past three months. The average price target for Tesla is $377.08, implying a 3.18% upside from the current price.

data.title: September Rate Hike Odds Surge Above 85% as Inflation Accelerates
data.description:
Rate hike odds at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting surged on Friday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published August's Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. During the month, the CPI rose 0.4%, up from 0.1% in July. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy items, advanced 0.3% compared to 0.2% in the prior month.

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike next week are now at 88.7%, up from 72.4% on Thursday and 59.4% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Fed Faces Balancing Act as Inflation Stays Elevated

Inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for over five years. Higher rates can help ease inflation by increasing borrowing costs and discouraging consumers and companies from spending.

data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Gains as David Ellison Has "Tricks Up His Sleeve" to Make the Merger Succeed
data.description:
For anyone giving up hope that the merger between entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) will go through, take hope. It turns out that Paramount CEO David Ellison has "tricks up his sleeve" to make the merger a reality, according to word from the New York Post. Only time will tell if any of them will work, but the idea is giving investors hope. Paramount shares gained nearly 2% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Paramount has seen a 41.47% loss in its share price over the past year.

Ways and Means, Plans and Schemes

One of the biggest tricks available, the report noted, is that Ellison can make Rob Bonta—California's Attorney General—seem as though he is "out of step with even lefty Dems." This actually is not as hard to do as you might think; given that New Jersey wants out of the lawsuit, finding more elements of the suit willing to turn against Bonta might not be hard.

Other tricks include pointing out that big tech firms might take aim at Warner instead, suggesting that someone will likely buy Warner, so why not someone who understands the market? And of course, there remains the specter of Paramount moving out of California altogether, which still could happen if Bonta doesn't start talking about solutions to settle this suit before it goes to trial in March 2027.

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Notches Up After Announcing $1 Billion Investment in Kentucky Truck Plant
data.description:
Legacy automaker Ford (F) took the recent criticism about it, and its connections to China, to heart, and delivered a big new investment in its operations. Ford is putting $1 billion into the Kentucky Truck Plant to demonstrate its belief in America, and by extension, itself. Investors were modestly pleased, and Ford shares gained fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen an 18.84% rally in its share price over the past year.

Painting Over the Problem

Ford's investment in the Kentucky Truck Plant will go into a new paint shop, according to a report from CNBC. Ford plans to break ground on the new shop by the end of the year, and will use the new paint shop to completely replace the old one. This will "…further [modernize] one of Ford's most important manufacturing operations," the report noted.

Ford also noted that the $1 billion going into the new paint shop is on top of the approximately $4 billion that Ford has already put into the Kentucky Truck Plant over the last few years. Then Ford made it clear why all this was going on, saying, "These investments demonstrate our confidence in Kentucky's workforce, our commitment to American manufacturing, and our belief that the future of mobility and energy will be built right here in the United States."

Maybe Don't Mock Ford for its China Connections?

A Bloomberg report, meanwhile, came out with the idea that calling Ford out on its Chinese connections might actually prove counter-productive. Basically, the report suggests, Ford is doing what it can with what it has to work with. If that means that Ford has to pull ideas from other countries in order to advance innovation, then perhaps those who think like Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy should back off and let Ford do the job.

The report goes on from there, declaring, "Shutting out Chinese battery technology altogether, even the licensing of it, won't create an all-American, world-beating battery industry; it will prevent one from forming. Similarly, there is an inherent tension between making vehicles affordable and making them entirely on US soil." Some might disagree with these assertions, but the fact they exist at all provides an indication of just what the overall climate looks like for Ford these days.

data.title: Viking Stock (VIK) Pops as Company Launches Hydrogen-Powered Cruise Ship
data.description:
The stock of Viking Holdings (VIK) is trending higher on Sept. 11 after the company announced progress with its first hydrogen-powered cruise ship. Called the "Viking Astrea," the new ship has been floated out of a shipyard in Italy. The ship is now undergoing interior outfitting and is on track for delivery in May 2027. The cruise ship is expected to undertake its first Mediterranean and Northern Europe trips next year.

The Astrea hydrogen-powered cruise ship provides zero emissions and is good for the environment, said the company. It uses a hybrid propulsion system built partly around liquefied hydrogen and fuel cells, with up to six megawatts of energy output. Viking said the new vessel can operate in environmentally sensitive areas without exhaust emissions.

Diesel Prices Hit Record Highs

Hydrogen ships generally store hydrogen onboard, either as compressed gas or cryogenic liquid hydrogen. In a fuel cell system, hydrogen combines electrochemically with oxygen from the air, producing electricity to run electric motors and ship systems. The hydrogen fuel cells are part of a broader propulsion arrangement, potentially alongside other onboard power sources, said Viking.

data.title: Trump's Proposed $5,000 Dividend to Americans Can Be 'Fiscally Responsible,' Says Hassett
data.description:
White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said Friday that President Trump's proposed $5,000 dividend to adult citizens in the U.S. can be "fiscally responsible" due to strong economic growth and high levels of wealth generation. Earlier this week, Trump said he would send the dividend if the Republicans win the November midterm elections. "It is a serious proposal," said Hassett.

The dividend, which would cost an estimated $1.35 trillion, immediately raised concerns of bringing inflation and the national debt higher.

National Debt at Record High as Inflation Stays Elevated

Inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), was 3.4% in August. Furthermore, the national debt is currently at a record-high $40 trillion and continues to climb.

data.title: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Gains as a New Backed Company Prepares for IPO
data.description:
Chip stock Intel (INTC) has been making some exciting progress as a company lately. It turns out that it is also making exciting progress as a company backer. We heard about Kepler Computing yesterday, but one more came to the forefront in a report from Reuters. Altera is setting up for an initial public offering (IPO) that could be worth $2 billion to the company. That news reflected well on Intel, and shares rose over 3% in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 316.61% rally in its share price over the past year.

Another Potential Winner

The report noted that Altera could be ready for its IPO before the end of this year, and would be one of the largest semiconductor listings of the last few years. Barclays is set to serve as underwriter for the IPO, but the order of the banks involved has not been finalized.

Better yet, it would also serve as reinforcement that the United States IPO market has been having a record year. The total IPO market stands at around $137 billion total raised through the end of August, and there are several other IPOs remaining that could emerge this year. Since Intel backed Altera before the IPO, it would likely receive a substantial portion of that release itself. Better yet, Altera makes a line of programmable chips currently in use in several fields, including the telecom market and the United States military.
